description: Update UI and documentation: replace login.html template with Microsoft sign-in button following branding guidelines, update .env.example with comprehensive Azure AD configuration documentation including redirect URI setup instructions emphasizing capital M
steps: Replace entire contents of app/templates/login.html: keep extends base.html and unauthenticated_content block structure; remove WTForms form; add Microsoft sign-in button with official styling (white background, gray border #8c8c8c, gray text #5e5e5e); add SVG four-color Microsoft logo (red #f25022, blue #00a4ef, green #7fba00, yellow #ffb900); button links to url_for('auth.microsoft_auth'); change heading from 'TAS ERP Login' to 'TR Portal Login' per original user request; add helper text about using company Microsoft account and contacting IT support

Update .env.example: add new section 'Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) SSO Configuration' with detailed comments; add AZURE_TENANT_ID with provided value as example; add AZURE_CLIENT_ID with provided value; add AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET with instructions to obtain from Azure Portal > Certificates & secrets; add APP_URL with examples for development (http://localhost:5000) and production (https://yourdomain.com); add optional rate limiting section with LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT, AUTH_INITIATE_RATE_LIMIT, AUTH_CALLBACK_RATE_LIMIT commented out with defaults; add important multi-line note about redirect URI configuration in Azure Portal emphasizing the exact URL format ${APP_URL}/auth/Microsoft/callback and that the M in Microsoft must be capitalized
acceptance_criteria: login.html displays 'TR Portal Login' heading (not 'TAS ERP')
login.html shows 'Sign in with Microsoft' button with correct Microsoft branding colors and four-square logo
No username/password form is visible in login.html
.env.example contains complete Azure AD configuration section with all required variables
.env.example includes clear instructions for obtaining client secret from Azure Portal
.env.example emphasizes redirect URI must use capital M in Microsoft
verification: Run: flask run, navigate to http://localhost:5000/login in browser, confirm page title is 'Login - TR Portal', heading shows 'TR Portal Login', Microsoft button is visible with four-color logo, no username/password fields are present
Run: cat .env.example | grep -A 20 'Microsoft Entra' and confirm Azure AD section exists with comprehensive documentation
Run: cat .env.example | grep 'Microsoft/callback' and confirm redirect URI examples include capital M
Run: cat .env.example | grep -i 'RATE_LIMIT' and confirm optional rate limiting configuration is documented
Visual inspection: open login page in browser and confirm Microsoft button styling matches design (white background, gray border, Microsoft logo colors correct)
findings: UI and documentation updates successfully implemented. login.html replaced with Microsoft SSO button design: heading changed from 'TAS ERP Login' to 'TR Portal Login' per original user request (message index 1), page title updated to 'Login - TR Portal', WTForms username/password form removed, Microsoft sign-in button added with official four-color logo (red #f25022, blue #00a4ef, green #7fba00, yellow #ffb900) and branding-compliant styling (white background, gray border #8c8c8c, gray text #5e5e5e), button links to url_for('auth.microsoft_auth'), helper text added about using company Microsoft account and contacting IT support. .env.example updated with comprehensive Azure AD SSO configuration section: AZURE_TENANT_ID and AZURE_CLIENT_ID documented with provided example values, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET with instructions to obtain from Azure Portal Certificates & secrets, APP_URL with examples for development (http://localhost:5000) and production (https://yourdomain.com), optional rate limiting configuration section added with LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT/AUTH_INITIATE_RATE_LIMIT/AUTH_CALLBACK_RATE_LIMIT commented out with default values, comprehensive multi-line redirect URI configuration note added emphasizing ${APP_URL}/auth/Microsoft/callback format with step-by-step Azure Portal instructions and explicit note that 'M' in Microsoft must be capitalized. All acceptance criteria met: heading shows 'TR Portal Login', Microsoft button with correct branding visible, links to /auth/microsoft route, no username/password fields present, .env.example contains complete Azure AD section with clear client secret instructions, redirect URI documentation emphasizes capital M, rate limiting configuration documented. Verification confirmed: redirect URI examples show capital M in Microsoft/callback, Azure AD section present with comprehensive documentation including tenant ID/client ID/client secret/APP_URL, rate limiting configuration documented with three configurable parameters.
